newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower in lackluster trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended down in weak, trendless trade Thursday despite a rise in electrical sector shares after the privatization of Bahia state utility Coelba, brokers said.
"The market is weak and people are having a hard time understanding why it is performing poorly," a trader at local Sintese brokerage told Reuters.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 47 most-trade issues fell 1.13 percent to end at 12,872 points on volume totalling 1.188 billion reais ($1.1 billion), according to preliminary figures.
Almost a third of total trade, which is close to the recent daily average, was attributable to the auction of shares of Sao Paulo state water and sewer utility Sabesp, brokers said.
Otherwise, trade was weak as speculation, light profit-taking and day trading by domestic investors combined to depress prices despite solid fundamentals, brokers said.
Investors may be feeling uneasy about changes at the Central Bank, where International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco is due to replace outgoing bank President Gustavo Loyola, they said.
The exception was power sector shares. The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index closed 1.83 percent higher at 3,628 points.
Preferred shares of Coelba soared after a controlling stake was sold on the Rio de Janeiro bolsa, closing up 6.1 percent at 87 reais.

Other electrical shares also rose. Sao Paulo state owned Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz' (CPFL) common closed up 2.31 percent at 221 reais while preferred shares of Cesp, also owned by Sao Paulo state, rose 5.45 percent at 81.50 reais.
Minas Gerais state's Cemig common ended 0.93 percent higher at 54 reais.

Although most power shares rose, Coelba common slid back 5.41 percent to end at 105 reais, adjusting to the sale price, and federal power holding Eletrobras' preferred B dropped back 1.39 percent to close at 640 reais.

Sabesp raised 406.7 million reais through the sale of 1.295 billion voting shares but the Sao Paulo bourse auction was only a moderate success as the stock went for 314 reais per 1,000 shares compared with the base price of 313 reais, traders said.
